children.title: Exact-Approximate Polyhedral Regimes
children.top_down_role: Exact and approximate computational regimes for rational polyhedra.

children.title: Weak Polyhedral Problems
children.top_down_role: Tolerance-based access to rational polyhedral regions.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a bounded closed convex set, \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb{Q}_{>0}\), and \(\|c\|_2\leq1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weak polyhedral problems permit outer feasibility error and optimize only against the eroded set, with additive objective error \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Points whose closed epsilon-ball lies in K.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean tolerance version of weak feasibility and weak maximization for bounded convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Weak feasibility at tolerance \(\varepsilon\) asks either for a point \(y\in K^{+\varepsilon}\) or for the correct assertion \(K^{-\varepsilon}=\varnothing\). Weak maximization additionally receives \(c\) with \(\|c\|_2\leq1\) and, unless \(K^{-\varepsilon}=\varnothing\), asks for \(y\in K^{+\varepsilon}\) satisfying \(c^Ty\geq c^Tx-\varepsilon\) for every \(x\in K^{-\varepsilon}\). Thus both geometric feasibility and objective optimality are interpreted with an explicitly encoded tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak problems accept points near the set and compare objective values against an eroded set, allowing a specified additive tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Polyhedral Problems

children.title: Strong Polyhedral Problems
children.top_down_role: Exact access to rational polyhedral data or decisions.

assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\leq b\}\) is a rational polyhedron and all queries are rational.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong problems require exact membership, exact separating inequalities, and exact optimal values or status certificates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact separation and optimization versions for rational polyhedra.

source_refs.locator: * 6.4 Equivalence of Strong Optimization and Separation p. 174

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Strong separation, given \(y\), must decide exactly whether \(y\in P\); if not, it returns rational \((a,\beta)\) such that \(a^Tx\leq\beta<a^Ty\) for every \(x\in P\). Strong optimization, given \(c\), must return an exact maximizer of \(c^Tx\) over \(P\) and its exact rational value when finite and attained, or correctly report infeasibility or unboundedness with the corresponding exact certificate. No geometric or objective tolerance is part of either specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong polyhedral problems demand exact membership and separation, or an exact optimizer and value, with exact certificates for infeasibility or unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Polyhedral Problems

children.title: Exact–Approximate Complexity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Representation and precision conditions separating the two problem regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact–Approximate Complexity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rational-gap boundary separating tolerance answers from recoverable exact polyhedral answers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Distinct reduced rational numbers with denominators at most \(Q\) differ by at least \(1/Q^2\). Therefore, if an approximation \(\widehat z\) to such a rational value \(z\) satisfies \(|\widehat z-z|<1/(2Q^2)\), then \(z\) is the unique rational with reduced denominator at most \(Q\) in that error interval and can be recovered by rational reconstruction. Without a known encoding or denominator bound, no fixed positive tolerance ensures exact recovery: for any \(\varepsilon>0\), choose a rational \(\delta\) with \(0<\delta<\varepsilon\). The intervals \(P_0=[0,1]\) and \(P_\delta=[0,1+\delta]\) admit a common \(\varepsilon\)-accurate maximization answer for objective \(c=1\), although their exact optimal values are \(1\) and \(1+\delta\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximation determines an exact rational answer when its error is strictly below half a known denominator-dependent gap; without such a bound, arbitrarily close polyhedra can have different exact optima.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\), and the exact rational value \(z\) has reduced denominator at most \(Q\).
\(\widehat z\) is an approximation to \(z\), and weak answers use a tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact recovery is guaranteed when \(|\widehat z-z|<1/(2Q^2)\); without a known size bound, fixed-tolerance weak information does not determine exact answers.

notation.meaning: Known upper bound on the reduced denominator of the exact rational value.
Approximation to the exact rational value z.

children.title: Precision Requirements
children.top_down_role: Bit precision needed for reliable polyhedral decisions or witnesses.

knowledge_statements.title: Precision Requirements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient absolute accuracy for exact membership decisions on integer inequality systems at rational query points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\), \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}\), \(A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{Z}^m\), and \(y\in\mathbb{Q}^n\). If \(q\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\) satisfies \(qy\in\mathbb{Z}^n\), then every slack \(s_i=b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}y\) belongs to \(q^{-1}\mathbb{Z}\). For approximations satisfying \(|\widetilde{s}_i-s_i|<1/(2q)\), one has \(s_i>0\) when \(\widetilde{s}_i>1/(2q)\), \(s_i<0\) when \(\widetilde{s}_i<-1/(2q)\), and \(s_i=0\) when \(|\widetilde{s}_i|<1/(2q)\). These alternatives decide exactly whether \(y\in P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an integer inequality system and a rational query with common denominator q, slack approximations with absolute error below 1/(2q) determine every slack sign, including zero, and therefore decide exact membership.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The approximations determine every slack sign and decide exactly whether \(y\in P\).

notation.meaning: slack of inequality i at the query point
a common denominator of the query coordinates

children.title: Geometric Radius Bounds
children.top_down_role: Inner-radius and outer-radius information governing geometric scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Radius Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An explicit outer-radius estimate for bounded polyhedra described by bounded integer data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\), \(A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{Z}^m\), and \(H\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}\), with \(|A_{ij}|\le H\) and \(|b_i|\le H\) for all indices. If \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}\) is nonempty and bounded, then every \(x\in P\) satisfies \(\|x\|_2\le\sqrt n\,n!H^n\). Equivalently, \(P\subseteq B(0,\sqrt n\,n!H^n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty bounded polyhedron in n dimensions whose integral inequality data have magnitude at most H lies in the Euclidean ball centered at zero with radius √n n! H^n.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}\), \(|A_{ij}|\le H\), and \(|b_i|\le H\) for all indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P\subseteq B\!\left(0,\sqrt n\,n!H^n\right).\]

notation.meaning: uniform magnitude bound on the integer input data
closed Euclidean ball centered at zero with radius R

children.title: Conditioning Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of oracle behavior on geometric conditioning.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lipschitz sensitivity of linear optimization values to Hausdorff perturbations of compact feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K,L\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty compact sets and let \(d_H(K,L)\le\delta\) under the Euclidean metric, where \(\delta\ge0\). Define \(h_K(c)=\max_{x\in K}c^{\mathsf T}x\) and \(h_L(c)=\max_{x\in L}c^{\mathsf T}x\). For every \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(|h_K(c)-h_L(c)|\le\|c\|_2\delta\). In particular, if \(\|c\|_2=1\), then \(|h_K(c)-h_L(c)|\le\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moving a nonempty compact feasible set by Hausdorff distance at most δ changes any linear optimum by at most the objective norm times δ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[|h_K(c)-h_L(c)|\le \|c\|_2\delta\quad\text{for every }c\in\mathbb{R}^n.\]

notation.meaning: support functions of K and L

children.title: Tolerance Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where rounding or separation tolerances obscure the intended conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A one-dimensional family showing that tolerance comparable to geometric feature size cannot preserve exact decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon>0\), let \(K_\varepsilon=[0,\varepsilon]\subset\mathbb{R}\) and \(y_\varepsilon=2\varepsilon\). Then \(y_\varepsilon\notin K_\varepsilon\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(y_\varepsilon,K_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon\). Under a weak-membership convention that permits an IN response whenever \(\operatorname{dist}(y,K)\le\delta\), the exterior query \(y_\varepsilon\) may receive IN for every \(\delta\ge\varepsilon\). For the objective \(c=1\), its candidate value \(c y_\varepsilon=2\varepsilon\) exceeds the exact optimum \(h_{K_\varepsilon}(c)=\varepsilon\) by \(\varepsilon\). Thus weak acceptance at this tolerance cannot certify exact membership or exact-feasible optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When tolerance is at least the width of a small interval, weak membership may accept an exterior point whose objective value exceeds the interval's true optimum by that width.
assumptions_latex: The weak-membership convention permits IN when \(\operatorname{dist}(y,K)\le\delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weak acceptance at tolerance \(\delta\ge\varepsilon\) need not certify exact membership or an exactly feasible optimizer over \(K_\varepsilon\).

children.title: Polyhedral Oracle Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Computational access models for explicitly or implicitly represented convex and polyhedral sets.

children.title: Membership-Validity Oracle Interface
children.top_down_role: Interfaces centered on point inclusion and universal inequality validity.

children.title: Point Membership
children.top_down_role: Oracle access centered on whether a query point lies in a region.

knowledge_statements.title: Point Membership
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact membership oracle for a specified convex or polyhedral feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a fixed set represented implicitly. An exact point-membership oracle accepts a query \(y\in\mathbb{Q}^n\) and returns YES precisely when \(y\in K\), and NO precisely when \(y\notin K\). When \(K=P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\) is explicitly represented, the predicate is equivalent to \(a_i^{\mathsf T}y\le b_i\) for every row \(i\). The oracle's output is exact: no tolerance band around the boundary is left unspecified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point-membership oracle decides exactly whether a rational query belongs to the fixed feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle returns YES if and only if \(y\in K\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimization Oracle Yields Strong Separation for a Rational Polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle reduction with explicit rationality, interior-point, and encoding-size hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,T\in\mathbb N\), \(y,x_0\in\mathbb Q^n\), and let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a rational polytope with \(x_0\in\operatorname{int}P\). Suppose \(\operatorname{size}(x_0)\le \log T\) and \(\operatorname{size}(x)\le \log T\) for every vertex \(x\) of \(P\). Given an oracle that, for every \(c\in\mathbb Q^n\), returns a vertex \(x^*\in P\) attaining \(\max\{c^\top x:x\in P\}\), the separation problem for \(P\) at \(y\) is solvable in time polynomial in \(n\), \(\log T\), and \(\operatorname{size}(y)\). If \(y\notin P\), the algorithm can return a facet-defining inequality of \(P\) violated by \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a rational polytope whose vertices and a known rational interior point have bounded encoding size, a linear-optimization oracle returning an optimal vertex can be converted into a polynomial-time separation algorithm. When the query point lies outside the polytope, the algorithm can produce a violated facet-defining inequality.
assumptions_latex: P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is a rational polytope}
\forall c\in\mathbb Q^n,\ \text{the oracle returns }x^*\in\operatorname{vert}(P)\text{ with }c^\top x^*=\max_{x\in P}c^\top x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{SEP}(P,y)\text{ is solvable in }\operatorname{poly}(n,\log T,\operatorname{size}(y))\text{ time, and if }y\notin P\text{ a violated facet-defining inequality can be returned.}

children.title: Inequality Validity
children.top_down_role: Oracle access centered on whether an inequality holds throughout a region.

knowledge_statements.title: Inequality Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact validity oracle for linear inequalities over a fixed feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be fixed. An exact inequality-validity oracle receives \((a,\beta)\in\mathbb{Q}^n\times\mathbb{Q}\) and returns YES precisely when \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) holds for every \(x\in K\). If \(K\) is nonempty and compact, this is equivalent to \(h_K(a)=\max_{x\in K}a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\). A NO answer asserts the existence of some \(x\in K\) with \(a^{\mathsf T}x>\beta\), although the interface need not return such a witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality-validity oracle decides whether a queried rational linear inequality holds at every point of the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle returns YES if and only if \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) for all \(x\in K\).

children.title: Membership–Validity Reductions
children.top_down_role: Conditions supporting computational transfer between the two interfaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Membership–Validity Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact membership–validity conversion through polar duality for convex bodies containing the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex with \(0\in\operatorname{int}K\), and define \(K^\circ=\{z:z^{\mathsf T}x\le1\text{ for all }x\in K\}\). The bipolar theorem gives \(K=(K^\circ)^\circ\). Hence a membership query \(y\in K\) is equivalent to validity of \(y^{\mathsf T}z\le1\) over \(K^\circ\). Conversely, for \(\beta>0\), validity of \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) over \(K\) is equivalent to membership \(a/\beta\in K^\circ\). Thus exact membership and positive-right-hand-side validity reduce to one another when the polar body is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polar duality converts membership in a convex body into validity over its polar, and positive-threshold validity into polar membership.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[y\in K\iff y^{\mathsf T}z\le1\ \forall z\in K^\circ,\qquad a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\ \forall x\in K\iff a/\beta\in K^\circ.\]

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The polar identities are mathematically standard, but the cited section is identified only as optimization from membership and is already flagged as possibly not stating this polar reduction. A source locator explicitly supporting the bipolar and membership–validity equivalences is required; the domains of y and a should also be stated when sourced.

children.title: Exact-Weak Separation Interface
children.top_down_role: Exact and approximate interfaces for identifying violated inequalities.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Violated, active, satisfying, and almost-satisfying cut sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions for a proper cut-requirement function and a selected edge set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g\) be a proper function on \(2^{V(G)}\), let \(F\subseteq E(G)\), and let \(X\subseteq V(G)\). The set \(X\) is violated with respect to \((g,F)\) iff \(|\delta_F(X)|<g(X)\). An active set is an inclusion-minimal violated set. The set \(F\) satisfies \(g\) iff no vertex set is violated, and it almost satisfies \(g\) iff \(|\delta_F(X)|\ge g(X)-1\) for every \(X\subseteq V(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vertex set is violated when too few selected edges cross its cut. Active sets are inclusion-minimal violated sets. The edge set satisfies the requirement when no set is violated, and almost satisfies it when every cut misses its requirement by at most one.
assumptions_latex: g\text{ is a proper function on }2^{V(G)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\text{ is violated}\iff |\delta_F(X)|<g(X);\quad F\text{ satisfies }g\iff \nexists X:\ |\delta_F(X)|<g(X);\quad F\text{ almost satisfies }g\iff \forall X\subseteq V(G),\ |\delta_F(X)|\ge g(X)-1.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uncrossing and disjointness of active sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncrossing structure when the selected edge set misses every proper-function cut requirement by at most one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g\) be a proper function and let \(F\subseteq E(G)\) almost satisfy \(g\). If \(A,B\subseteq V(G)\) are violated, then either both \(A\setminus B\) and \(B\setminus A\) are violated, or both \(A\cap B\) and \(A\cup B\) are violated. Consequently, any two distinct active sets with respect to \((g,F)\) are disjoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an edge set that almost satisfies a proper cut requirement, two violated sets uncross into either two violated differences or a violated intersection and union. Hence distinct inclusion-minimal violated sets are disjoint.
assumptions_latex: A,B\subseteq V(G)\text{ are violated with respect to }(g,F)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(A\setminus B\text{ and }B\setminus A\text{ are violated}\bigr)\ \lor\ \bigl(A\cap B\text{ and }A\cup B\text{ are violated}\bigr);\quad A',B'\text{ distinct active}\Rightarrow A'\cap B'=\varnothing.

children.title: Exact Separation
children.top_down_role: Exact identification of containment or a separating inequality.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact strong separation oracle for a nonempty compact convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex. An exact separation oracle receives \(y\in\mathbb{Q}^n\). If \(y\in K\), it returns IN. If \(y\notin K\), it returns \((a,\beta)\in\mathbb{Q}^n\times\mathbb{Q}\) such that \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta<a^{\mathsf T}y\) for every \(x\in K\). No tolerance band is permitted in either output alternative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty compact convex set, exact separation either confirms membership or returns a rational valid inequality strictly violated by the rational query.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is IN with \(y\in K\), or \((a,\beta)\in\mathbb{Q}^n\times\mathbb{Q}\) with \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta<a^{\mathsf T}y\) for every \(x\in K\).

children.title: Weak Separation
children.top_down_role: Tolerance-based separation for approximate geometric access.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-based separation with a specified Euclidean near-membership alternative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(\delta>0\). A \(\delta\)-weak separation oracle queried at \(y\in\mathbb{Q}^n\) may return NEAR only when \(\operatorname{dist}(y,K)\le\delta\). Otherwise it returns a vector \(a\in\mathbb{Q}^n\) with \(\|a\|_2=1\) satisfying \(a^{\mathsf T}y\ge h_K(a)+\delta\), where \(h_K(a)=\sup_{x\in K}a^{\mathsf T}x\). Thus queries farther than \(\delta\) receive a valid separating direction with margin at least \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak separation may declare a point near the set within δ; farther points receive a normalized separator with margin at least δ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle returns NEAR with \(\operatorname{dist}(y,K)\le\delta\), or \(a\) with \(\|a\|_2=1\) and \(a^{\mathsf T}y\ge h_K(a)+\delta\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Weak-separation conventions vary materially. The cited full text must confirm this particular combination of Euclidean near-membership, unit rational output, and margin at least δ. For a general closed unbounded convex set, existence of the stipulated rational unit separator is also not established by the supplied citation.

children.title: Separation Precision Boundary
children.top_down_role: Geometric and encoding conditions controlling transfer between exact and weak access.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation Precision Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The rational slack gap separating sufficient precision from an unavoidable weak-oracle ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\), \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}\), \(A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{Z}^m\), and \(y\in\mathbb{Q}^n\). If \(q\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\) satisfies \(qy\in\mathbb{Z}^n\), then every violated row satisfies \(a_i^{\mathsf T}y-b_i\ge1/q\), and row-evaluation error strictly below \(1/(2q)\) preserves the sign of every nonzero violation. This scale is sharp up to the factor two: for \(P=(-\infty,0]\subset\mathbb{R}\) and \(y=1/q\), the violation and distance to \(P\) both equal \(1/q\). Under a weak-separation convention permitting NEAR whenever \(\operatorname{dist}(y,P)\le\delta\), \(\delta\ge1/q\) therefore does not require a separating output for this exterior query.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a rational query with common denominator q, nonzero row violations are at least 1/q, so evaluation error below 1/(2q) preserves their signs, while near-set tolerance at least 1/q can hide an exterior point.
assumptions_latex: The weak-separation convention permits NEAR when \(\operatorname{dist}(y,P)\le\delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Evaluation precision strictly below \(1/(2q)\) detects every nonzero row violation, whereas ambiguity tolerance \(\delta\ge1/q\) cannot guarantee a separating output in general.

notation.meaning: common denominator of the query coordinates

children.title: Exact-Weak Optimization Interface
children.top_down_role: Exact and approximate objective-based access to implicit regions.

children.title: Exact Optimization
children.top_down_role: Objective-based access requiring an exact optimum or exact status.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linear-optimization oracle over a nonempty compact feasible set, with rational objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and compact. An exact linear-optimization oracle receives \(c\in\mathbb{Q}^n\) and returns \(x^*\in K\) satisfying \(c^{\mathsf T}x^*=\max_{x\in K}c^{\mathsf T}x\), together with the exact optimal value if the interface requests it. If \(K\) is a rational polytope, an optimal rational vertex can be returned. The output requires exact feasibility and exact objective optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact optimization returns a feasible point attaining the true maximum of the queried rational linear objective; for a rational polytope, a rational optimal vertex can be selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(x^*\in K\) satisfies \(c^{\mathsf T}x^*=\max_{x\in K}c^{\mathsf T}x\).

children.title: Weak Optimization
children.top_down_role: Approximate objective-based access under explicit tolerances.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive-error linear optimization with exact feasibility over a compact feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and compact. Given \(c\in\mathbb{Q}^n\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), an additive \(\varepsilon\)-weak optimization oracle returns \(x_\varepsilon\in K\) such that \(c^{\mathsf T}x_\varepsilon\ge h_K(c)-\varepsilon\), where \(h_K(c)=\max_{x\in K}c^{\mathsf T}x\). This convention relaxes objective optimality by an absolute amount \(\varepsilon\) but retains exact feasibility. If objectives are normalized by \(\|c\|_2=1\), the tolerance has the same geometric scale as Euclidean perturbations of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak optimization returns an exactly feasible point whose objective is within additive ε of the true linear optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(x_\varepsilon\in K\) satisfies \(c^{\mathsf T}x_\varepsilon\ge h_K(c)-\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed additive-error definition is internally coherent, but weak-optimization conventions differ, and the cited GLS formulation may permit approximate feasibility rather than require xε∈K exactly. Full-text confirmation of this exact-feasibility convention is needed before the mathematical interface can be accepted.

children.title: Optimization Precision Boundary
children.top_down_role: Encoding and scale conditions governing equivalence between exact and weak access.

assumptions_latex: \(L\in\mathbb{N}\) is part of the rational input-size parameter.
Approximate maximization uses the additive guarantee \(c^{\mathsf T}x\geq h_K(c)-\varepsilon\), where \(h_K(c)=\max_{z\in K}c^{\mathsf T}z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varepsilon\)-optimization implies exact optimization only when additional data provide a positive lower bound on the gap between distinct attainable objective values, and \(\varepsilon\) is smaller than that bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive weak optimization cannot generally recover an exact rational optimum without a precision bound tied to encoding size.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Complexity, Oracles, and Numerical Computation p. 21

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K_L=\{0,2^{-L}\}\subset\mathbb{R}\) and objective \(c=1\), the exact optimum is \(2^{-L}\). If \(\varepsilon\geq 2^{-L}\), then returning \(x=0\) satisfies \(x\geq \max_{z\in K_L}z-\varepsilon\), although it is not exactly optimal. Hence a weak optimization oracle with tolerance independent of \(L\) does not determine the exact optimum. More generally, conversion from weak to exact optimization requires a known objective-value separation bound derived from rational encoding or comparable discrete structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak optimization yields an exact optimum only when its tolerance is below a known gap between distinct attainable objective values.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimization Precision Boundary

children.title: Separation Witness Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Oracle interfaces distinguished by witness form and tolerance regime.

children.title: Violation Detection
children.top_down_role: Interfaces reporting whether a candidate inequality or point violates the region.

knowledge_statements.title: Violation Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Boolean detection is distinguished from producing a separating witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact violation-detection oracle for \(K\) maps each query \(y\) to one of two outputs: \(\mathrm{ACCEPT}\) if \(y\in K\), and \(\mathrm{REJECT}\) if \(y\notin K\). Its specification requires only correct evaluation of the membership predicate. A rejection need not include coefficients \((a,\beta)\) satisfying \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta<a^{\mathsf T}y\) for every \(x\in K\); producing such coefficients is the stronger separating-witness task.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Violation detection answers whether a query point belongs to the convex set, without necessarily returning a separating hyperplane.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a specified closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output determines whether \(y\in K\) but supplies no separating inequality when membership fails.

children.title: Separating-Witness Output
children.top_down_role: Interfaces returning an explicit geometric certificate of exclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Separating-Witness Output
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong separation certificate for a point outside a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A separating-witness output for \(y\) is a pair \((a,\beta)\in(\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\})\times\mathbb{R}\) such that \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) for every \(x\in K\), while \(a^{\mathsf T}y>\beta\). Positive rescaling leaves the represented halfspace unchanged, so the witness may be normalized by \(\lVert a\rVert_2=1\). The strict inequality places \(y\) outside a valid halfspace containing all of \(K\), thereby certifying \(y\notin K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separating witness is a valid inequality containing the entire convex set but strictly violated by the query point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((a,\beta)\) is a mathematical certificate that \(y\notin K\).

notation.meaning: normal vector of the separating inequality
right-hand side of the separating inequality

children.title: Approximate Violation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Violation interfaces parameterized by numerical or geometric tolerances.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Violation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean additive tolerance with an explicit indifference band.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A \(\delta\)-approximate violation detector for \(K\), where \(\delta>0\), must return \(\mathrm{ACCEPT}\) whenever \(y\in K\), and must return \(\mathrm{REJECT}\) whenever \(\operatorname{dist}(y,K)\geq\delta\), where \(\operatorname{dist}(y,K)=\inf_{x\in K}\lVert y-x\rVert_2\). For queries satisfying \(0<\operatorname{dist}(y,K)<\delta\), either answer is allowed. Exact violation detection is the separate regime in which every query outside \(K\) must be rejected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate detection must accept members and reject points at least delta away, but may answer arbitrarily within the intervening tolerance band; exact detection rejects every nonmember.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Correct output is mandatory for \(y\in K\) and for \(\operatorname{dist}(y,K)\geq\delta\), while either output is permitted when \(0<\operatorname{dist}(y,K)<\delta\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean distance from the query to the set

children.title: Witness-Strength Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Comparative information content of violation and separation outputs.

assumptions_latex: Witness normals are normalized by \(\lVert a\rVert_2=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A larger certified margin is a stronger witness; every positive-margin witness implies violation detection, but a Boolean rejection contains no witness coefficients.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Witnesses are ordered by certified normalized separation margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a valid normalized witness \((a,\beta)\), define its margin at \(y\) by \(m(a,\beta;y)=a^{\mathsf T}y-\beta\). If \(m(a,\beta;y)\geq\gamma>0\), the witness is a \(\gamma\)-strong certificate and implies \(\operatorname{dist}(y,K)\geq\gamma\). Consequently, a \(\gamma_2\)-strong witness also meets every weaker requirement \(0<\gamma_1\leq\gamma_2\). An unquantified strict witness certifies only some positive margin, while a Boolean violation output certifies no explicit halfspace or margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized witnesses are stronger when they certify a larger margin; any such witness detects violation, while a Boolean rejection supplies no hyperplane.
knowledge_statements.title: Witness-Strength Comparisons

children.title: Optimization–Separation Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Landmark reduction family connecting implicit optimization and separation access.

children.title: Convex-Body Oracle Equivalences
children.top_down_role: Weak oracle equivalences for general convex bodies under geometric access conditions.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a convex body with known rational \(a\), \(0<r\leq R\), and \(B_2(a,r)\subseteq K\subseteq B_2(a,R)\).
All queries and requested tolerances have finite rational encodings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weak separation and weak linear optimization for \(K\) are polynomial-time oracle reducible to one another under these geometric access bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-bounded full-dimensional convex bodies in the weak, rational oracle model.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Complexity, Oracles, and Numerical Computation p. 21

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the stated sandwiching bounds, an oracle solving weak separation over \(K\) can be used to compute, for any rational \(c\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), a point whose objective value is within \(\varepsilon\) of \(\sup_{x\in K}c^{\mathsf T}x\). Conversely, weak optimization can implement weak separation with polynomially related tolerances. The numbers of arithmetic operations and oracle calls are polynomial in \(n\), the input encoding length, \(\log(R/r)\), and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex body with known inner and outer radius bounds, weak separation and weak optimization simulate each other in polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Body Oracle Equivalences

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 1. Complexity, Oracles, and Numerical Computation p. 21

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The claimed equivalence depends on the precise definitions of weak separation, weak optimization, feasibility slack, and tolerance conversion. Those conventions are neither stated nor inspectably supported by the supplied locations, so the theorem's exact hypotheses and conclusion cannot yet be validated.

children.title: Rational-Polyhedral Oracle Equivalences
children.top_down_role: Strong equivalences supported by rational encoding and bounded certificate size.

knowledge_statements.title: Rational-Polyhedral Oracle Equivalences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong oracle equivalence for bounded, well-described rational polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty bounded rational polyhedron with a known facet-complexity bound \(L\). Strong separation over \(P\) and exact rational linear optimization over \(P\) are polynomial-time oracle reducible to one another. The bit complexity and number of oracle calls are bounded by a polynomial in \(n\), \(L\), and the binary encoding length of the objective vector or query point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a bounded rational polyhedron with a known facet-complexity bound, exact linear optimization and strong separation implement one another in oracle-polynomial time.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty bounded rational polyhedron.
A facet-complexity bound \(L\) for a rational inequality description of \(P\) is known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong separation and exact rational linear optimization over \(P\) are polynomial-time oracle equivalent, with complexity polynomial in \(n\), \(L\), and the query encoding length.

children.title: Oracle-Reduction Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Ellipsoid-mediated and related transformations among polyhedral access problems.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq B_2(a,R)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is convex and accessed by a valid separation oracle.
The objective \(c\in\mathbb{Q}^n\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ellipsoid reduction returns an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal feasible point, or a valid emptiness conclusion under the adopted weak-feasibility convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ellipsoid-mediated reduction from separation to weak linear optimization.

source_refs.locator: * 6.4 Equivalence of Strong Optimization and Separation p. 174

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(E_0=B_2(a,R)\) and an empty incumbent list. At iteration \(k\), query the center \(z_k\). If separation returns \(u^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta<u^{\mathsf T}z_k\), replace \(E_k\) by the minimum-volume standard ellipsoidal update containing \(E_k\cap\{x:u^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\}\). If \(z_k\) is feasible, retain it and use an objective cut based on \(c^{\mathsf T}x\). Stop when the maintained objective bounds differ by at most \(\varepsilon\), and output the best retained feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ellipsoid method alternates separating and objective cuts until its objective bounds are within tolerance, then returns the best feasible center found.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Reduction Mechanisms

source_witnesses.locator: * 6.4 Equivalence of Strong Optimization and Separation p. 174

These omissions affect both termination and correctness, so the mathematical version requires source-backed reconstruction.

children.title: Oracle Equivalence Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by missing geometric bounds, encoding control, precision, or adequate oracle information.

children.title: Missing Radius Bounds
children.top_down_role: Oracle-reduction limits caused by absent inner-scale or outer-scale control.

assumptions_latex: An ellipsoid-based reduction is expected to run in time polynomial in the available input parameters.
No positive inner-radius bound \(r\), or equivalent width parameter, is supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No complexity guarantee polynomial only in \(n\), \(\log R\), and requested accuracy follows from the standard well-bounded-body reduction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The standard weak-oracle reduction needs quantitative well-boundedness, not merely boundedness.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Complexity, Oracles, and Numerical Computation p. 21

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The usual ellipsoid oracle bound contains a term proportional to \(\log(R/r)\) when \(B_2(a,r)\subseteq K\subseteq B_2(a,R)\). If only \(R\) is known, convex bodies may have arbitrarily small inradius while all stated parameters remain fixed. The quantity \(\log(R/r)\) is then unbounded and the volume-shrinkage stopping argument supplies no uniform polynomial iteration bound. Lower-dimensional bodies correspond to \(r=0\) in the ambient space and require separate affine-hull or rational-encoding information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without an inner-radius or comparable width bound, standard ellipsoid reductions have no uniform polynomial iteration guarantee, especially for thin or lower-dimensional bodies.
knowledge_statements.title: Missing Radius Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 1. Complexity, Oracles, and Numerical Computation p. 21

children.title: Uncontrolled Encoding Size
children.top_down_role: Reduction failures caused by insufficient rational representation bounds.

assumptions_latex: The feasible sets are rational and exact output is required.
No upper bound on coefficient, facet, or vertex encoding length is included in the complexity parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weak accuracy cannot be converted uniformly to exact output, and strong oracle reductions need not have polynomial bit complexity in the stated parameters.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact polynomial equivalence depends on counting and bounding rational bit complexity.

source_refs.locator: * 6.4 Equivalence of Strong Optimization and Separation p. 174

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(P_L=[0,2^{-L}]\subset\mathbb{R}\) and maximize \(x\). Its exact optimum has encoding length proportional to \(L\), and distinguishing it from \(0\) by additive optimization requires \(\varepsilon<2^{-L}\). If \(L\) is uncontrolled and omitted from the input-size measure, neither the necessary precision nor the output length is polynomially bounded by dimension alone. Thus exact optimization-separation equivalence requires an explicit rational encoding-complexity bound or an equivalent certificate-size bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If rational encoding length is uncontrolled, exact optima and separating certificates may require unbounded precision and output size even in one dimension.
knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Encoding Size

source_witnesses.locator: * 6.4 Equivalence of Strong Optimization and Separation p. 174

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded thickening and volume bound for rational linear feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative reduction of rational linear feasibility to a bounded, full-dimensional relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{Q}^m\), \(S=\operatorname{size}(A)+\operatorname{size}(b)\), \(\mathbf 1\) be the all-one vector, \(\epsilon^{-1}=2n\,2^{4S}\), and \(R=1+2^{4S}\). Then \(Ax\le b\) is feasible if and only if \(Ax\le b+\epsilon\mathbf 1\) and \(-R\mathbf 1\le x\le R\mathbf 1\) are jointly feasible. Moreover, if \(Ax\le b\) is feasible, then
\[\operatorname{vol}_n\!\left(\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b+\epsilon\mathbf 1,\ -R\mathbf 1\le x\le R\mathbf 1\right\}\right)\ge\left(\frac{2\epsilon}{n2^{\operatorname{size}(A)}}\right)^n.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a rational inequality system, explicit bounds determined by its encoding length produce a bounded relaxed system that is feasible exactly when the original system is feasible. When the original system is feasible, the bounded relaxation also has the stated positive lower bound on its n-dimensional volume.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ax\le b\text{ is feasible}\iff\exists x:\ Ax\le b+\epsilon\mathbf 1,\ -R\mathbf 1\le x\le R\mathbf 1;\quad Ax\le b\text{ feasible}\Rightarrow\operatorname{vol}_n(P_{\epsilon,R})\ge\left(\frac{2\epsilon}{n2^{\operatorname{size}(A)}}\right)^n.

children.title: Precision-Limited Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Limits on oracle transfer under inadequate numerical accuracy.

assumptions_latex: The available oracle is guaranteed correct only to a fixed tolerance \(\delta>0\).
The requested optimization or separation accuracy is \(\varepsilon<\delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fixed-precision oracle does not, without refinement access or discrete gap information, imply an oracle solving the target task to accuracy \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle equivalence transfers accuracies only through an explicit polynomial tolerance relation.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Complexity, Oracles, and Numerical Computation p. 21

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Weak-oracle reductions invoke their source oracle at tolerances determined by the desired target accuracy. If access is restricted to a fixed \(\delta\), admissible answers may conceal geometric or objective differences smaller than \(\delta\). For example, the intervals \(K_0=[-1,0]\) and \(K_1=[-1,\eta]\), with \(0<\eta<\delta\), have support values in direction \(1\) differing by \(\eta\); a \(\delta\)-accurate response need not distinguish them. Hence it cannot guarantee optimization error \(\varepsilon<\eta/2\) without finer queries or gap information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-tolerance oracle cannot generally support reductions demanding finer accuracy because geometries and objective values below its resolution may remain indistinguishable.
knowledge_statements.title: Precision-Limited Equivalence

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 1. Complexity, Oracles, and Numerical Computation p. 21

children.title: Information-Deficient Oracles
children.top_down_role: Non-equivalence regimes caused by oracle outputs too weak for the desired reduction.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) ranges over general closed convex sets.
The oracle returns only a Boolean membership or violation answer and exposes neither a hyperplane nor quantitative distance information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Boolean rejection alone is not a separating certificate, and no unrestricted strong-separation reduction follows without additional geometric, encoding, or refinement assumptions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical output insufficiency of Boolean detection for strong witness production in an unrestricted oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rejected query \(y\notin K\), a Boolean oracle reveals only the truth value of \(y\in K\). Strong separation instead requires explicit \((a,\beta)\) satisfying \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta<a^{\mathsf T}y\) for all \(x\in K\), with representable coefficients and controlled size. The Boolean answer contains none of these data. Transforming repeated Boolean answers into such a witness therefore requires additional assumptions, such as quantitative radius bounds, finite-precision refinement, rational encoding bounds, or a specified richer oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Boolean rejection does not itself reveal a separating hyperplane; witness recovery requires additional geometric, precision, encoding, or oracle-access assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Information-Deficient Oracles

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between a Boolean rejection and an explicit separating witness is correct, but the broader nonreducibility assertion depends on the allowed query model, precision, adaptivity, and representation of K. The cited oracle-definition location does not inspectably establish that boundary.

children.title: Combinatorial Convex Hulls
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral representations generated by incidence vectors of discrete feasible objects.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex hull of edge-incidence vectors of all 1-trees in a complete graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(V(K_n)=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), the convex hull of the incidence vectors of all 1-trees is
\[\left\{x\in[0,1]^{E(K_n)}:\sum_{e\in E(K_n)}x_e=n,\ \sum_{e\in\delta(1)}x_e=2,\ \sum_{e\in E(K_n[X])}x_e\le |X|-1\quad\forall\,\varnothing\ne X\subseteq\{2,\ldots,n\}\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The 1-tree polytope consists exactly of edge vectors between zero and one whose total edge weight is n, whose weight on edges incident to vertex 1 is two, and whose internal edge weight on every nonempty subset X of vertices 2 through n is at most |X|-1.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}\{\chi^{E(T)}:T\text{ is a 1-tree}\}=\left\{x\in[0,1]^{E(K_n)}:\sum_e x_e=n,\ \sum_{e\in\delta(1)}x_e=2,\ \sum_{e\in E(K_n[X])}x_e\le |X|-1\ \forall\varnothing\ne X\subseteq\{2,\ldots,n\}\right\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear optimization over a combinatorial convex hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality of linear optimization values over a set family and the convex hull of its incidence vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((E,\mathcal F)\) be a set system, let \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^X:X\in\mathcal F\}\), and let \(c:E\to\mathbb R\). With \(c(X)=\sum_{e\in X}c(e)\), one has \(\max\{c^\top x:x\in P\}=\max\{c(X):X\in\mathcal F\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing a linear objective over the convex hull of a family's incidence vectors has the same value as maximizing the corresponding set weight over the family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{x\in P}c^\top x=\max_{X\in\mathcal F}c(X).

children.title: Natural Continuous Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Canonical outer polyhedral descriptions derived from discrete models.

knowledge_statements.title: Natural Continuous Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard LP relaxation obtained by dropping integrality while retaining the linear constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{Q}^m\). For the integer feasible set \(S=\{x\in\mathbb{Z}^n:Ax\le b\}\), its natural continuous relaxation is the rational polyhedron \[R=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}.\] Thus \(S=R\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\) and \(S\subseteq R\). All linear constraints, including any variable bounds, equalities, and sign restrictions in the formulation, remain in \(R\); only the requirement \(x\in\mathbb{Z}^n\) is replaced by \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The natural continuous relaxation retains every linear constraint but permits the integer variables to take real values, producing a rational polyhedron containing every integer-feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=R\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\subseteq R\)

children.title: Integer Hulls
children.top_down_role: Convex-hull representations of integer feasible points.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Hulls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer hull of a rational polyhedron in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rational polyhedron \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), its integer hull is \[R_I=\operatorname{conv}(R\cap\mathbb{Z}^n).\] It is the smallest convex set containing every integral point of \(R\). Moreover, \(R_I\subseteq R\), and the integer hull of a rational polyhedron is itself a rational polyhedron. If \(R\cap\mathbb{Z}^n=\varnothing\), the convention is \(R_I=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The integer hull is the convex hull of all integral points in a rational polyhedron; it is contained in the relaxation and is again rational polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_I=\operatorname{conv}(R\cap\mathbb{Z}^n)\subseteq R\)

notation.meaning: integer hull of the polyhedron R

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dominating-Integer-Point Characterization of the Integrality Ratio
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization of an integrality-ratio bound by componentwise domination of an integer-hull point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R_+^n\) be a rational polyhedron and let \(r\ge0\). The integrality ratio of \(P\) is at most \(r\) if and only if, for every \(x\in P\), there exists \(y\in P_I\) such that \(rx\ge y\) componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative rational polyhedron has integrality ratio at most r exactly when every point of the relaxation, scaled by r, componentwise dominates some point of its integer hull.
assumptions_latex: P\subseteq\mathbb R_+^n\text{ is a rational polyhedron}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{ir}(P)\le r\iff\forall x\in P\;\exists y\in P_I:\;rx\ge y\text{ componentwise}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedrality of an integral-data integer hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concerns the convex hull of integer solutions to a feasible system of linear inequalities with integral coefficients and right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\in\mathbb Z^{m\times n}\) and \(d\in\mathbb Z^m\), assume \(\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Dx\ge d\}\neq\varnothing\), and define \(X=\{x\in\mathbb Z^n:Dx\ge d\}\). Then \(\operatorname{conv}(X)\) is a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible system of linear inequalities with integral data, the convex hull of its integer solutions is a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(X)\text{ is a polyhedron}\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundedness Equivalence for a Rational Polyhedron and Its Integer Hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of upper boundedness over a rational polyhedron and its nonempty integer hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\) be a rational polyhedron with nonempty integer hull \(P_I\), and let \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). Then \(\max\{cx:x\in P\}\) is bounded above if and only if \(\max\{cx:x\in P_I\}\) is bounded above.

children.title: Relaxation Exactness
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes where a natural relaxation coincides with the discrete hull.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness relative to all integer points admitted by a rational polyhedral relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a rational polyhedron and let \(S=R\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\). The relaxation is exact precisely when \[R=\operatorname{conv}(S)=R_I.\] Under this condition, for every \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), whenever the minima exist, \[\min\{c^Tx:x\in R\}=\min\{c^Tx:x\in S\}.\] Thus every linear objective has zero additive relaxation gap, although an optimal point returned over \(R\) need not itself be integral when the optimal face has positive dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation is exact when it equals the convex hull of its integer points, so every attained linear optimum agrees with the integer optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R=\operatorname{conv}(S)\)

children.title: Relaxation Gap Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Settings where continuous descriptions depart from integer-hull geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Gap Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative gap for nonnegative minimization and a one-variable unbounded-gap family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem with integer feasible set \(S\subseteq R\), objective \(c^Tx\ge0\), and positive finite relaxation optimum, define \[\gamma(R,S,c)=\frac{\min\{c^Tx:x\in S\}}{\min\{c^Tx:x\in R\}}\ge1.\] Exactness gives \(\gamma=1\) for every such objective, but containment alone gives no finite universal bound. Indeed, for \(0<\varepsilon<1\), take \(S_\varepsilon=\{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}:x\ge\varepsilon\}\), \(R_\varepsilon=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}:x\ge\varepsilon\}\), and minimize \(x\). Then the integer optimum is \(1\), the relaxation optimum is \(\varepsilon\), and \(\gamma=1/\varepsilon\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation gap is the integer optimum divided by the positive relaxed optimum. Without additional structure, even one-variable natural relaxations have unbounded multiplicative gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{0<\varepsilon<1}\gamma(R_\varepsilon,S_\varepsilon,1)=\infty\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The multiplicative-gap convention and one-variable unbounded-gap family are mathematically coherent, and failure_boundary fits the leaf, but neither claim has a cited source.

children.title: Packing-Covering Blocker Duality
children.top_down_role: Monotone polyhedral systems organized by packing, covering, and blocker duality.

children.title: Packing Polyhedra
children.top_down_role: Downward-monotone polyhedral structures arising from packing systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Packing Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative linear packing systems with componentwise nonnegative data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^m\). The associated packing polyhedron is \[P(A,b)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^n:Ax\le b\}.\] It is downward closed in the nonnegative orthant: if \(x\in P(A,b)\) and \(0\le y\le x\) componentwise, then \(y\in P(A,b)\). Consequently, packing objectives are conventionally maximized with nonnegative objective coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A packing polyhedron consists of nonnegative vectors consuming no more than available nonnegative resources and is closed under componentwise decreases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in P(A,b),\ 0\le y\le x\Longrightarrow y\in P(A,b)\)

children.title: Covering Polyhedra
children.top_down_role: Upward-monotone polyhedral structures arising from covering systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Covering Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative linear covering systems with componentwise nonnegative coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^m\). The associated covering polyhedron is \[C(A,b)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^n:Ax\ge b\}.\] It is upward closed in the nonnegative orthant: if \(x\in C(A,b)\) and \(y\ge x\) componentwise, then \(y\in C(A,b)\). Covering objectives are therefore conventionally minimized with nonnegative objective coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A covering polyhedron consists of nonnegative vectors meeting nonnegative requirements and is closed under componentwise increases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in C(A,b),\ y\ge x\Longrightarrow y\in C(A,b)\)

children.title: Blocking Polyhedra
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral structures organized through blocker representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Blocking Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upward-comprehensive polyhedra in the nonnegative orthant, normalized to exclude the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A blocking polyhedron is a nonempty polyhedron \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^n\) satisfying \[Q+\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^n=Q\] and \(0\notin Q\). Equivalently, whenever \(x\in Q\) and \(y\ge x\) componentwise, one has \(y\in Q\). The exclusion of the origin ensures that inequalities of the form \(z^Tx\ge1\), with \(z\ge0\), can define a nontrivial blocker.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A blocking polyhedron is a nonempty nonnegative polyhedron closed under coordinatewise increases and excluding the origin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q+\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^n=Q\) and \(0\notin Q\)

children.title: Blocker Duality
children.top_down_role: Geometric correspondences connecting monotone polyhedral families.

knowledge_statements.title: Blocker Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Involutive blocker operation on nonempty blocking polyhedra excluding the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a blocking polyhedron \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^n\), define its blocker by \[B(Q)=\{y\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^n:y^Tx\ge1\text{ for every }x\in Q\}.\] Then \(B(Q)\) is a blocking polyhedron and the blocker operation is involutive: \[B(B(Q))=Q.\] It also reverses inclusion: for blocking polyhedra \(Q_1,Q_2\), \(Q_1\subseteq Q_2\) implies \(B(Q_2)\subseteq B(Q_1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The blocker contains nonnegative vectors pairing to at least one with every original point. Blocking twice recovers the original polyhedron, and inclusion is reversed.

children.title: Canonical Graphical Polyhedra
children.top_down_role: Canonical graph-derived polyhedral families retained as foundational examples.

children.title: Network-Flow Polyhedra
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral structures derived from flows, circulations, or network incidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Network-Flow Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacitated directed-flow polyhedron and its integral-data integrality property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,E)\) be a finite directed graph, let \(N\) be its node-arc incidence matrix, and let \(b\in\mathbb{R}^V\) satisfy \(\sum_{v\in V}b_v=0\). Given bounds \(\ell,u\in\mathbb{R}^E\) with \(\ell\le u\), the capacitated flow polyhedron is \[F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^E:Nx=b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}.\] If \(b,\ell,u\) are integral, then every nonempty face of \(F\) contains an integral point; in particular, every vertex of \(F\) is integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A network-flow polyhedron enforces flow balance and arc bounds. Integral supplies, demands, and bounds yield integral vertices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\{x:Nx=b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\), with integral vertices for integral data

children.title: Matching Polyhedra
children.top_down_role: Convex-hull structures associated with graph matchings.

knowledge_statements.title: Matching Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Edmonds's description of the matching polytope for a finite undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\), let \(P_M(G)\) be the convex hull of incidence vectors of matchings. Then \[P_M(G)=\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^E:x(\delta(v))\le1\ \forall v\in V,\quad x(E(S))\le\frac{|S|-1}{2}\ \forall S\subseteq V\text{ with }|S|\text{ odd}\right\}.\] Here \(x(F)=\sum_{e\in F}x_e\), \(\delta(v)\) is the set of edges incident with \(v\), and \(E(S)\) contains edges having both ends in \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The matching polytope is described by nonnegativity, degree constraints, and odd-set constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_M(G)=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^M:M\subseteq E\text{ is a matching}\}\) equals the displayed system

notation.meaning: edges with both endpoints in S

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed Edmonds matching-polytope description is mathematically standard and representation is the correct role, but this nontrivial theorem has no citation or inspectable locator.

children.title: Spanning-Tree Polyhedra
children.top_down_role: Convex-hull structures associated with spanning trees.

knowledge_statements.title: Spanning-Tree Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-inequality description of the spanning-tree polytope of a connected graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite connected undirected graph. The spanning-tree polytope, the convex hull of incidence vectors of spanning trees, is \[P_{ST}(G)=\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^E:x(E)=|V|-1,\quad x(E(S))\le |S|-1\ \forall\,\varnothing\ne S\subsetneq V\right\}.\] Here \(x(F)=\sum_{e\in F}x_e\), and \(E(S)\) denotes the edges with both endpoints in \(S\). Every vertex of this polytope is the incidence vector of a spanning tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The spanning-tree polytope uses nonnegativity, total edge weight equal to one less than the vertex count, and forest inequalities on every proper vertex subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{ST}(G)=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^T:T\text{ is a spanning tree of }G\}\) equals the displayed system

notation.meaning: edges with both endpoints in S

children.title: Stable-Set Polyhedra
children.top_down_role: Convex-hull structures for mutually nonadjacent vertex selections.

knowledge_statements.title: Stable-Set Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-hull definition and basic valid inequalities for stable sets of a graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\), a stable set is a vertex subset containing no edge. Its stable-set polytope is \[\operatorname{STAB}(G)=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^S\in\{0,1\}^V:S\subseteq V\text{ is stable}\}.\] Every point \(x\in\operatorname{STAB}(G)\) satisfies \(x_v\ge0\) for all \(v\in V\) and \(x(C)\le1\) for every clique \(C\) of \(G\). These basic inequalities need not describe \(\operatorname{STAB}(G)\) completely for an arbitrary graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stable-set polytope is the convex hull of stable-set incidence vectors. Nonnegativity and clique inequalities are valid but may be insufficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{STAB}(G)=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^S:S\text{ is stable}\}\)

notation.meaning: sum of coordinates indexed by clique C

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex-hull definition and validity and insufficiency of the listed basic inequalities are standard and correctly scoped, but the record supplies no source or locator.

children.title: Coloring Polyhedra
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral representations of graph color assignments or partitions.

assumptions_latex: \(q\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}\) is a fixed number of labeled colors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{COL}_q(G)=\operatorname{conv}\{x\in\{0,1\}^{V\times[q]}:x_{vk}+x_{wk}\le 1\ \forall vw\in E,\ k\in[q],\ \sum_{k=1}^q x_{vk}=1\ \forall v\in V\}\).

notation.meaning: Color-assignment coordinate, equal to one when vertex \(v\) receives color \(k\).
Convex hull of incidence vectors of proper labeled \(q\)-colorings of \(G\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the fixed-number, labeled-color assignment formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each proper coloring \(c:V\to[q]\), let \(x^c_{vk}=1\) exactly when \(c(v)=k\). The fixed-\(q\) coloring polyhedron is the polytope
\[\operatorname{COL}_q(G):=\operatorname{conv}\{x^c:c\text{ is a proper }q\text{-coloring of }G\}.\]
Equivalently, its generating binary vectors satisfy \(\sum_{k=1}^q x_{vk}=1\) for every \(v\in V\) and \(x_{vk}+x_{wk}\le 1\) for every \(vw\in E\) and \(k\in[q]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coloring polyhedron is the convex hull of binary assignment vectors that give every vertex one color and give adjacent vertices different colors.
knowledge_statements.title: Coloring Polyhedra

children.title: Cut Polyhedra
children.top_down_role: Convex-hull structures generated by graph cuts.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{CUT}(G)=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^{\delta(S)}:S\subseteq V\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{E}\).

notation.meaning: Edge cut having one endpoint in \(S\) and the other in \(V\setminus S\).
Incidence vector of the edge set \(\delta(S)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the undirected graph cut polytope in edge space.

source_refs.locator: 3.1 The Max-Flow and Min-Cut Problems p. 116
source_refs.source_title: Network Optimization: Continuous and Discrete Models

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(S\subseteq V\), define \(\delta(S):=\{uv\in E:|\{u,v\}\cap S|=1\}\), and let \(\chi^{\delta(S)}\in\{0,1\}^{E}\) be its incidence vector. The cut polytope of \(G\) is
\[\operatorname{CUT}(G):=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^{\delta(S)}:S\subseteq V\}.\]
Because \(\delta(S)=\delta(V\setminus S)\), complementary shores generate the same vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cut polytope is the convex hull of edge-incidence vectors of all vertex bipartition cuts of a finite undirected graph.

children.title: Conflict–Partition Relations
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondences among conflict, coloring, and cut representations.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c\longleftrightarrow(c^{-1}(1),\ldots,c^{-1}(q))\) is a bijection between proper labeled \(q\)-colorings and ordered stable-set partitions of \(V\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the labeled-coloring and stable-set-partition correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A map \(c:V\to[q]\) is a proper coloring if and only if its fibers \(S_k:=c^{-1}(k)\) are stable sets satisfying \(S_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}S_q=V\), where empty fibers are allowed. Thus proper labeled \(q\)-colorings correspond bijectively to ordered stable-set partitions. Under incidence vectors, the coloring vector is the concatenation \((\chi^{S_1},\ldots,\chi^{S_q})\), so the coloring polytope is the convex hull of these partition encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper labeled coloring is exactly an ordered partition of the vertices into stable sets, with empty color classes allowed.
knowledge_statements.title: Conflict–Partition Relations

children.title: Rank-System Polyhedral Family
children.top_down_role: Polyhedra generated by independence, bases, rank, and submodular systems.

children.title: Matroid Independence Polyhedra
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral structures generated by independent sets.

assumptions_latex: \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) is a finite matroid with rank function \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_I(M)=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^I:I\in\mathcal I\}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^{E}:x(S)\le r(S)\ \forall S\subseteq E\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-matroid independence polytope with its rank-inequality description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The independence polytope of \(M\) is
\[P_I(M):=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^I:I\in\mathcal I\}.\]
For a finite matroid it has the exact rank description
\[P_I(M)=\{x\in\mathbb R_{\ge 0}^{E}:x(S)\le r(S)\text{ for every }S\subseteq E\},\]
where \(x(S):=\sum_{e\in S}x_e\). Its vertices are precisely the incidence vectors of independent sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The matroid independence polytope is the convex hull of independent-set vectors and equals the nonnegative region defined by all rank inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Independence Polyhedra

children.title: Matroid Base Polyhedra
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral structures generated by bases.

assumptions_latex: \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) is a finite matroid with rank function \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B(M)=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^B:B\text{ is a base of }M\}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^{E}:x(S)\le r(S)\ \forall S\subseteq E,\ x(E)=r(E)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-matroid base polytope as a maximum-cardinality face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The base polytope of \(M\) is
\[B(M):=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^B:B\text{ is a base of }M\}.\]
It is the face of the independence polytope on which total cardinality is maximal, and hence
\[B(M)=\{x\in\mathbb R_{\ge 0}^{E}:x(S)\le r(S)\text{ for every }S\subseteq E,\ x(E)=r(E)\}.\]
Its vertices are precisely the incidence vectors of bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The matroid base polytope is the convex hull of base vectors, equivalently the rank-inequality region restricted by total weight equal to the matroid rank.
knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Base Polyhedra

children.title: Polymatroid Polyhedra
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral structures arising from submodular rank data.

assumptions_latex: \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R\) is normalized, nondecreasing, and submodular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(f)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^{E}:x(S)\le f(S)\ \forall S\subseteq E\}\), and \(B(f)=P(f)\cap\{x:x(E)=f(E)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the normalized, monotone submodular set-function convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Normalization, monotonicity, and submodularity mean \(f(\varnothing)=0\), \(f(S)\le f(T)\) whenever \(S\subseteq T\), and \(f(S)+f(T)\ge f(S\cup T)+f(S\cap T)\). The associated polymatroid polyhedron is
\[P(f):=\{x\in\mathbb R_{\ge 0}^{E}:x(S)\le f(S)\text{ for every }S\subseteq E\}.\]
Its base polytope is \(B(f):=\{x\in P(f):x(E)=f(E)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized, nondecreasing, submodular set function defines a polymatroid through nonnegativity and one upper-bound inequality for every subset; its base polytope is the face on which the total coordinate sum equals the function value of the ground set.
knowledge_statements.title: Polymatroid Polyhedra

children.title: Rank-System Correspondences
children.top_down_role: Connections between rank descriptions, base structures, and submodular geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) is a finite matroid with rank function \(r\).

notation.meaning: Matroid rank function \(r(S)=\max\{|I|:I\subseteq S,\ I\in\mathcal I\}\).
Polymatroid polyhedron induced by the rank function.
Base polytope induced by the rank function.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies matroid polyhedra as the integral polymatroids induced by matroid rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The matroid rank function \(r(S):=\max\{|I|:I\subseteq S,\ I\in\mathcal I\}\) is integer-valued, normalized, nondecreasing, and submodular. Its polymatroid satisfies
\[P(r)=\{x\in\mathbb R_{\ge 0}^{E}:x(S)\le r(S)\text{ for every }S\subseteq E\}=P_I(M).\]
Moreover, \(B(r)=P(r)\cap\{x:x(E)=r(E)\}=B(M)\). Thus the independent-set and base incidence vectors are respectively the vertices of these two integral polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid rank function defines a polymatroid whose polyhedron and base face are exactly the matroid independence and base polytopes.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-System Correspondences

children.title: Polyhedral Inequality Strengthening Calculus

children.title: Inequality Strength Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Classification of inequalities by correctness, comparative strength, and necessity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimal Inequality Descriptions Correspond to Facets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the inequalities and facets of a relatively full-dimensional polyhedron having a minimal inequality description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b\}\) be a nonempty polyhedron with \(\dim P=n-\operatorname{rank}(A)\). If \(A'x\leq b'\) is a minimal inequality system such that \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ A'x\leq b'\}\), then every inequality of \(A'x\leq b'\) is facet-defining for \(P\), and every facet of \(P\) is defined by an inequality of this system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty polyhedron that is full-dimensional in its equality affine space, every inequality in a minimal description defines a facet, and every facet is represented by one of those inequalities.
assumptions_latex: P\subseteq\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b\}\text{ is a nonempty polyhedron}
A'x\leq b'\text{ is a minimal inequality system}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every inequality of }A'x\leq b'\text{ is facet-defining for }P,\text{ and every facet of }P\text{ is defined by one of these inequalities}

children.title: Inequality Validity
children.top_down_role: Correctness status of inequalities relative to a target region.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^Tx\le\beta\) is valid for \(P\) if and only if \(P\subseteq\{x:a^Tx\le\beta\}\), equivalently \(\sup_{x\in P}a^Tx\le\beta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity is stated relative to an arbitrary nonempty polyhedron.

source_refs.locator: 4.1 Linear inequality systems and polyhedra p. 136

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The inequality \(a^Tx\le\beta\) is valid for \(P\) precisely when every \(x\in P\) satisfies it. Equivalently,
\[P\subseteq\{x\in\mathbb R^n:a^Tx\le\beta\},\]
or, using the extended-real supremum, \(\sup_{x\in P}a^Tx\le\beta\). If equality is attained by some point of \(P\), the valid inequality is supporting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality is valid for a polyhedron exactly when every point of the polyhedron satisfies it.
knowledge_statements.title: Inequality Validity

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1 Linear inequality systems and polyhedra p. 136

children.title: Inequality Dominance
children.top_down_role: Comparative strength among valid inequalities or descriptions.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a fixed reference relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^Tx\le\beta\) dominates \(c^Tx\le\delta\) relative to \(Q\) exactly when \(Q\cap H_1\subseteq Q\cap H_2\).

notation.meaning: Reference relaxation before either inequality is imposed.
Halfspaces defined by the first and second inequalities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses set-inclusion dominance relative to a specified relaxation.

source_refs.locator: 4.1 Linear inequality systems and polyhedra p. 136

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Relative to \(Q\), the inequality \(a^Tx\le\beta\) dominates \(c^Tx\le\delta\) when
\[Q\cap\{x:a^Tx\le\beta\}\subseteq Q\cap\{x:c^Tx\le\delta\}.\]
Dominance is strict when this inclusion is proper. Mutual dominance means the inequalities induce the same restricted feasible set on \(Q\), even if their coefficients are not proportional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One inequality dominates another relative to a relaxation when imposing the first leaves a subset of the points left by imposing the second.
knowledge_statements.title: Inequality Dominance

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1 Linear inequality systems and polyhedra p. 136

children.title: Inequality Redundancy
children.top_down_role: Dispensability of inequalities within a polyhedral description.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(Q:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^Tx\le\beta\) is redundant for \(Q\) if and only if \(Q=Q\cap\{x:a^Tx\le\beta\}\), equivalently \(\sup_{x\in Q}a^Tx\le\beta\).

notation.meaning: Nonempty polyhedron defined by the retained inequality system.
Candidate inequality whose addition or removal is tested.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Redundancy is relative to a nonempty remaining inequality system.

source_refs.locator: 4.1 Linear inequality systems and polyhedra p. 136

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The inequality \(a^Tx\le\beta\) is redundant relative to the system \(Ax\le b\) when adding it does not change the feasible region:
\[Q=Q\cap\{x\in\mathbb R^n:a^Tx\le\beta\}.\]
Because \(Q\) is nonempty, this is equivalent to validity of the candidate inequality for \(Q\), or to \(\sup_{x\in Q}a^Tx\le\beta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality is redundant relative to a nonempty remaining system when adding or removing it leaves the represented polyhedron unchanged; equivalently, the inequality is valid for that polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.title: Inequality Redundancy

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1 Linear inequality systems and polyhedra p. 136

children.title: Strength Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Ordering structures connecting validity, dominance, and redundancy.

assumptions_latex: Each candidate inequality \(h\) defines a halfspace \(H_h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_1\succeq_Q h_2\iff Q\cap H_{h_1}\subseteq Q\cap H_{h_2}\) defines a preorder, and its equivalence classes form a partial order under induced containment.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orders inequalities by inclusion of their restricted feasible regions.

source_refs.locator: 4.1 Linear inequality systems and polyhedra p. 136

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For candidate inequalities \(h_1,h_2\), define \(h_1\succeq_Q h_2\) exactly when \(Q\cap H_{h_1}\subseteq Q\cap H_{h_2}\). This relation is reflexive and transitive. Define \(h_1\sim_Q h_2\) when both dominance directions hold. Then dominance induces a partial order on the equivalence classes under \(\sim_Q\); strict containment gives strict strength, while an inequality valid for all of \(Q\) occupies the weakest equivalence class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative dominance is a preorder; after identifying inequalities that leave the same feasible set, it becomes a partial hierarchy ordered by strength.
knowledge_statements.title: Strength Hierarchies
